messages:
Alex: Heads up — started seeing a bunch of multi-GPU jobs fail in us-east-1-dc3 this morning with NCCL timeouts. First noticed ~03:10 UTC when training jobs hit repeated `unreachable peer` errors.

Alex: Error snippet:```
[0] NCCL WARN Could not reach peer 10.2.3.5:16197: No route to host
[0] NCCL WARN NCCL Network I/O errors, transport failed
[0] NCCL INFO Cleaning up communicators
```

Sam: Is this limited to a rack or random hosts? Any recent infra changes (firmware/drivers/switch config)?

Alex: Seems clustered around rack r3 (hosts r3-{01..08}). We did apply a Mellanox firmware push last night to R3 but only targeted users flagged for maintenance — cc @Mira to confirm.

Mira: I pushed mlx5 driver update + fw on r3 last night at 01:00 UTC (rollout job `fw-rollout-r3`). I rolled back for two hosts that failed quick smoke, but the rest reported healthy. No switch config changes on my end.

Sam: Can you grab a couple diagnostics from an affected and unaffected host? Key things: `ip link`, `ethtool -S`, `ibv_devinfo`, and `dmesg | tail`. MTU mismatch or offloads often bite RoCE/NCCL.

Alex: Collected from r3-05 (bad) and r3-10 (ok):
```
# r3-05 (bad)
ip link show eth0
3: eth0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1500 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether 7a:... brd ff:...

ethtool -S eth0 | head
    rx_packets: 1234567
    tx_packets: 1234500
    rx_errors: 14
    tx_errors: 0
ibv_devinfo -v
    hca_id: mlx5_2
    port 1: state PORT_ACTIVE

dmesg | tail -n 20
    mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0: firmware too old, uptime warnings
    mlx5_core: DRV Event: Port state change to ERR_EXCEED
```

```
# r3-10 (ok)
ip link show eth0
3: eth0: ... mtu 9000 ...
ethtool -S eth0 | head
    rx_packets: 2234567
    rx_errors: 0
ibv_devinfo -v
    hca_id: mlx5_0
    port 1: state PORT_ACTIVE
dmesg | tail -n 20
    no mlx5 warnings
```

Mira: Interesting — r3-10 is MTU 9000, r3-05 is 1500. That MTU mismatch between hosts (or between host and TOR) will wreck RoCE packets and lead to NCCL timeouts. We should have enforcement for jumbo frames on RDMA pools.

Jordan: That explains east-west packet drops. Did the firmware rollout change default MTU? It shouldn't, but maybe NIC auto-negotiated after fw change.

Sam: Also seeing `rx_errors` on the bad host. Could be switch path dropping fragmented RoCE frames when MTU isn't consistent. Need to check TOR config and intermediate links: verify `show interfaces` on TOR for MTU and PFC settings. RoCEv2 needs PFC/Egress priorities for lossless behavior.

ops-bot: ALERT: Grafana (net.r3.dc3) spike: interface drops + packet_loss for r3 cluster from 03:05–03:25 UTC — https://grafana.company/redwood/d/net-r3

Alex: Quick mitigation: pause scheduling of multi-GPU jobs on r3, and create a canary pool with MTU 9000 hosts only. I'll patch k8s nodeSelector for gpu-mtu=9000.

Mira: Agreed. I'll also run `ethtool -G eth0 rx 4096 tx 4096` and sync MTU to 9000 on r3-05..08, but we need to coordinate with network so we don't create blackholes.

Sam: Checklist to remediate:
- Validate physical path MTU: `ping -s $size -M do` across hosts and TOR
- Confirm TOR & spine MTU = 9000
- Check PFC config on switches (priority map for RoCE DSCP)
- Check mlx5 firmware consistency and roll back if required
- Add preflight MTU check to the driver/firmware rollout job

Jordan: For immediate capacity needs: I'll move critical jobs to us-east-1-dc1 where we have spare GPU pools. That buys time for patching.

Mira: One more thing — GPUDirect RDMA requires NIC <-> GPU DMA mappings. If host MTU changes after driver update, DPDK/ibverbs issues can pop up. I want to run `rdma link` and `ib_read_bw` between GPUs once MTU fixed.

Sam: If anyone opens a vendor ticket, include `ethtool -S`, `ibv_devinfo`, `dmesg`, and the `fw-rollout-r3` job id. That'll speed up vendor triage (Mellanox/Mellanox support asks for exact fw versions).

Alex: Action items assigned: Mira — coordinate with network on MTU & PFC and run host fixes (ETA 2 hours). Sam — add MTU check to rollout job + blametest infra change (ETA EOD). Jordan — shift critical workloads (in progress). Alex — create incident doc and schedule postmortem (ETA today).

Mira: I'll also snapshot one affected host and test a rollback of the mlx5 fw if hosts don't recover after MTU sync.

Sam: One more note: if we see persistent fragmentation issues despite MTU=9000 everywhere, check UDP segmentation offload (GSO/GRO) — sometimes offloading combined with RDMA causes weird behavior; temporarily disabling `gro`/`gso` on the RDMA interfaces can help debug.

Alex: Thanks all. Keep updates in this thread and tag me for any vendor ticket numbers. :thumbsup:
